**Lines 97, 113, 141-143, 177-178, 197-198** - SQL INJECTION EVERYWHERE!

You're saving raw credit card numbers to the database AND returning them in JSON responses. This is a PCI-DSS violation that'll get you fined into oblivion. Never store full PANs! Use tokenization!

## HIGH SEVERITY

**Lines 130-136** - Same goroutine disaster in CancelOrder. Also captures loop variables incorrectly - `productID` and `quantity` will all be the LAST values when goroutines execute!

**Line 55-59** - Response body never closed on inventory check. Resource leak that'll exhaust connections.

**Lines 171-172** - ProcessRefund allows ANY amount. I could request a $10,000 refund on a $5 order. No validation!

**Line 173** - Another SQL injection in the refund_log INSERT with the `Reason` field.

**Line 147** - Query error logged but processing continues with nil rows. Panic incoming!

**Line 50** - Trusting client-provided prices. I'll just set item.Price to -$1000 and you'll PAY ME to take your products!
